items.title: Ernest "Kid" Milton Interview, 1961-04-26
items.q: Well, George Lewis worked with me a good while. Before he had a band, George Lewis worked with me.

ctx.x: Are there any other clarinet players you liked besides Piku?

Well, George Lewis worked with me a good while. Before he had a band, George Lewis worked with me. How about Big Eye Lewis? Big Eye Lewis, I played with him a while. He worked with me a while. Because see, them fellas never had any work, now he should allow all of them a chance.
I want to ask you a question. This place where you work, is there any relative to the Lucherton that burned down?

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-11-01
items.q: Ernest Milton, myself, this member of it. We had played in two nights

ctx.x: One thing you talked about before, it was often the tablecorder run out, so if you could mention it again, you were saying when you were playing these last jobs with Buddy Buddy to see before he died. Can you tell about that? See, I was reading in two books. Two different books I was reading in the book by Sam Chardin and the book by Al Rose. They say that there was some picnic or something in Mandeville or something like that. I don't know what that was. No. I don't know what that was. No.

You better, you better, there wasn't no picnic until a child. Third, second, third, fourth of July. Goddamn, look, don't you betcha anymore, yeah? Yeah? You get out there? Yeah. Uh, no, it wasn't, it wasn't no picnic. We had played, uh, Longstoker, 48, two singles, uh, uh, Ernest Milton, myself, this member of it. We had played in two nights, come back every morning. Where were you playing? Empire, down Empire, down below the river on the sides, uh, you know, going towards the mountain river. And, uh, that…
He was actually dead by that.
